verdict: key partly consistent: 87 signs = 86 letters + 1 surplus (the plain stroke S24 inside ومال), 19 groups = 19 words; one letter per shape; two letters with two shapes (د: S14 and S20; ج/ن look-alikes S5/S11 kept apart at 3x). Both bayts are present; the 5r l.1-2 rows belong to the chain
notes: Rows 4v l.8-13 (l.10 is cipher, the segmenter calls it naskh) and 5r l.1-2 (black signs; the grey naskh around them is show-through from 5v). By eye 10+12+10+11+10+11+13+10 = 87 signs incl. the surplus stroke (record 11,12,10,11,11,11,16,12 = 94; its 5r figures came from an overlay that took show-through as signs), 19 dividers (record 19; 4v l.12 opens with one). The 5r rows continue حديثكم (S3 ك at the end of 4v l.13, S6 م at the start of 5r l.1) and carry سرور ومال والمروه والجاه, so they belong here and the fit is exact: the record's 'first verse missing' is wrong, the page text is the two bayts. Record plaintext corrected from the groups: (1) بخمر is بالخمر (6 signs: ب ا ل خ م ر; S9 ا and S10 ل as in الناس); (2) سادر is a 5-sign word ending in ي (S7, the ي of جميع, ثمانيه, هي, وطيب, حديثكم): read سادتي 'my lords', with S15 = ت a singleton (an ر would need a second ر shape; S4 is ر 5 times); (3) ها: is ها هي, two groups of two (S17 ه, S9 ا | S17 ه, S7 ي); (4) والمرق is والمروه (والمروءة without hamza; 7 signs, S1 و and S17 ه). Look-alike pairs checked at 3x: S12 (triangle, ب, 5x) vs S17 (open hook with loop, ه, 5x); S5 (ج: جميع, والجاه) vs S11 (ن: الناس, ثمانيه); S3 (cup on base, ك) vs S6 (pronged cup with tail, م, 6x incl. جميع, بالخمر, ثمانيه, حديثكم, ومال, والمروه). د has two shapes: S14 in سادتي and حديثكم, S20 in وشدا. Unexplained: S24, a long undotted stroke between م and ا of ومال on 5r l.1, with a black interlinear mark above it (a ر-like curve over show-through); counted as a surplus sign, not keyed; it is not a divider (no dots) and the word is complete without it.
